correctness.rationale: Rank-one mixed duality exactly reduces all measurable B to a section-size moment functional. For p<q, a uniform high/low split bounds both moments; the explicit two-height B_t,c saturates the limiting sharp maximum. For p>q, conjugate duality is exact. The binary expectation is squeezed between P_B and P_B plus a uniformly bounded complement; ordinary Lp handles p=q. A standalone numeric diagnostic is supplementary, not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact setwise averaging constant is a natural invariant governing the averaging-friendly hypothesis for Köthe-Banach targets. Optimizing all measurable atoms in the classical two-exponent mixed Lebesgue family yields a sharp blow-up exponent and nontrivial leading coefficient, and the same constant controls binary conditional expectations. This is structurally stronger than a qualitative counterexample and is naturally motivated by current operator-theoretic questions; finite-t optimizers remain open.
